signin-intro: Use the user name and password of your account on the computer that runs Private AI Framework. Only members of its pai group can sign in.
signin-required: Sign in to see this page.
signin-session-ended: Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.
signin-failed: Signing in failed. Try again; if it keeps failing, the web service may not be running.
signin-insecure: This connection is not encrypted, so your password is sent over the network as plain text. To keep it private, sign in on the computer that runs Private AI Framework, or only over a network you trust.
api-session-bad-credentials: The user name or password is not correct.
api-session-too-many-attempts: Too many attempts. Try again in {0} seconds.
api-session-unavailable: Signing in is not available on this server right now.
api-session-not-administrator: Only members of the pai group can sign in, and this account is not one. Ask whoever administers this computer to add it.
session-revoked: You have been signed out: this account is no longer a member of the pai group. Ask whoever administers this computer to add it again.
instance-label-hint: A name of your own for this instance, shown in the menu, on the overview and on this page. Leave it empty to name the instance by its engine and port again. The ID does not change.
instance-label-cleared: The label is removed: the instance is named {0} again.
instance-tags-hint: Labels you give this instance to tell it apart; they change nothing in how it runs or which requests reach it. Add one with the + button, using a-z, 0-9 and -; each change is saved at once. The tags of its server profile are shown below and are not changed here.
instance-tag-shown: {0} is already a tag of this instance.
server-profile-intro: llama-server settings of the instance that runs this server profile, shared by every model it serves ({0}). Per-model settings belong to the model profiles.
server-load-failed: The server settings could not be read.
server-profiles-intro: Each server profile holds the llama-server settings of one instance: its port, its addresses, its tags and the rest. An instance runs one server profile, and a server profile serves one instance at a time.
server-profiles-failed: The server profiles could not be read.
server-profiles-empty: There are no server profiles yet.
server-profile-name-hint: 1 to 32 characters: a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or a digit. It names the file server@<name>.ini and cannot be changed later.
server-profile-port-hint: The network port llama-server listens on. Filled in with the first port from 9931 up that no server profile uses; change it if you like. Two instances cannot run on the same address and port.
create-unknown: The manager did not answer in time, so it may or may not have been created. The list shows it if it was.
server-profile-not-found: There is no server profile named {0}.
server-profile-delete-question: Delete the server profile {0}? Its settings file is removed, with any unsaved changes on this page. This cannot be undone.
server-folder-unused-default: unset: the instance that runs this profile uses its own folder
api-client-not-authorized: Not authorized: the system refused this request.
api-client-unavailable: The Private AI manager service is not running or not reachable.
api-client-server-profile-exists: The server profile {0} is already there.
api-client-server-profile-in-use: The server profile {0} is already used by instance {1}.
api-client-no-server-profile: There is no server profile of that name.
api-server-profile-bad-id: invalid server profile id `{0}`: use lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting with a letter or digit, up to 32 characters
api-unknown-engine: unknown engine `{0}`: this manager serves the engine llama.cpp
server-snapshots-intro: Saves each loaded model's KV cache (its memory of the conversation) to disk when the server stops, and restores the newest one on the next start, so a restart need not read the whole conversation again. On a long prompt that takes far longer than reading the snapshot back. Off by default: a snapshot uses as much disk as the KV cache it holds, stopping waits for the write, and the next start loads the model right away to restore it.
server-sdk-intro: Settings of the GPU vendor's own libraries, passed to llama-server as environment variables at launch. They are not llama.cpp flags: nothing checks their values, and each one only affects its own backend.
server-cuda-nothing: Nothing to tune: the CUDA builds this framework ships need no workaround here.
server-hipblaslt-hint:
Chooses which of its two libraries ROCm uses for heavy matrix work. Leave it at default unless BF16 or F16 models crash.
Set it off on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) when every BF16/F16 model aborts on its first prefill batch. That happens only with the graphics driver's HIP runtime, which a Windows build from source uses; the installer puts ROCm's own runtime beside llama-server, so an installed framework should not need this.
default = don't set the variable: rocBLAS chooses (hipBLASLt for 16-bit work on RDNA4).
on = hipBLASLt; off = Tensile.
No effect on CUDA or Vulkan builds.
Variable: ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT
server-port-hint:
The network port llama-server listens on. The chat UI and integrations connect here.
Default: 9931 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --port
server-bind-to-hint:
Which addresses llama-server listens on. Check one or more.
localhost = only the computer running the server.
0.0.0.0 = every interface, reachable from your network. It covers all the other rows, so checking it clears them.
The chat UI and integrations connect to a loopback address when one is checked, otherwise to the first one.
Flag: --host
server-bind-localhost: localhost (only the computer running the server)
server-base-url-hint:
The address integrations use (opencode.json and Claude Code).
Default: built from host and port, with /v1 added for opencode.json; the default shown is that of the saved settings. Untick default to enter your own, for a proxy or gateway.
server-api-key-hint:
The key integrations send. Needed only behind a proxy or LLM gateway that requires one.
No key = none.
server-cpu-threads-hint:
How many CPU threads generate tokens. More won't help once the GPU is the limit.
Default: llama.cpp uses the physical core count. Maximum = the logical processors of the computer running the server.
Flag: --threads
server-batch-threads-hint:
How many CPU threads read the prompt (prefill).
Default: the same as CPU threads. Maximum = the logical processors of the computer running the server.
Flag: --threads-batch
server-max-models-hint:
How many models can stay loaded at once. 1 = one at a time, lowest VRAM; higher switches between models without reloading. 0 = no limit.
Default: 4 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --models-max
server-memory-margin-hint:
Memory kept free on every GPU, in MiB. Before loading a model, llama-server unloads the least recently used ones until the new one fits, on top of Max models.
Default: 0, off (llama.cpp's own): only Max models limits what stays loaded.
Flag: --models-memory-margin
server-models-folder-hint:
The folder holding your models, on the computer running the server. The pickers read its subfolders: models, mmprojs, mtps and dflashs.
Left empty, the instance uses its own folder, shown in the field.
server-web-ui-hint:
Serves the built-in chat page at /. With it off, the API keeps working.
Default: on (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --no-ui
server-mcp-proxy-hint:
Lets the built-in chat page reach MCP servers through llama-server, for those a browser cannot call directly. Each MCP server opts in with Use llama-server proxy in the chat page.
Anyone who can reach this server can then make it fetch any web address. Experimental in llama.cpp: keep it off on a network you do not trust.
Not passed while Web UI is off; your choice is kept.
Default: off (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --webui-mcp-proxy
server-mcp-proxy-toggle: serve the web UI's MCP proxy endpoint
server-log-level-hint:
How much llama-server writes to its log. Each level includes the ones below it: OUTPUT:0 writes almost nothing, DEBUG:5 everything.
Default: TRACE:4, which records each request in the instance's log. DEBUG:5 also logs the per-tensor lines tools\report-memory.ps1 reads.
Flag: --log-verbosity
server-save-on-shutdown-hint:
Saves the conversation to the snapshot folder when llama-server stops, and restores it at the next start. Worth it for long agent sessions, pointless for short prompts.
One file per loaded model, overwritten each time; files of models no longer loaded are removed.
Default: off.
Flag: --slot-save-path
server-save-on-shutdown-toggle: snapshot the KV cache on stop and restore it on start
server-snapshot-folder-hint:
Where snapshots go. A snapshot is about the size of the KV cache in use: it grows with the tokens actually in the conversation, NOT with Context size (a model's guide gives its size per token). Expect more on a hybrid model or with a drafter.
The default is on the system drive: point it at a data disk if that is tight.
The folder is created at launch: llama.cpp refuses to start without it.
Flag: --slot-save-path
server-profiler-attach-hint:
Lets ROCm's profiler (rocprofv3 --attach <pid>, in the TheRock dist) attach to the running llama-server. Only for profiling; without it the attach is refused.
Unchecked = don't set the variable.
No effect on CUDA or Vulkan builds.
Variable: ROCP_TOOL_ATTACH=1
server-allreduce-hint:
How the GPUs combine their results under split mode tensor. Applies to the whole server, CUDA and ROCm alike; no effect in other split modes.
Leave it at default, except for a tensor split that MIXES a CUDA and a ROCm GPU: that needs none, or the model aborts while loading. Prefill then falls well behind the layer split, with the same decode (the Radeon AI PRO R9700 guide has the figures).
default = don't set the variable: on Linux the collective library when the build links one (RCCL for ROCm), then the internal method; on Windows the internal one.
nccl = the collective library (RCCL on ROCm; NCCL on CUDA where the build found it).
internal = ggml's own method, through pinned host memory, so the slower card's PCIe link limits it.
none = the generic method of llama.cpp's meta backend.
Variable: GGML_CUDA_ALLREDUCE
server-gpu-graphs-hint:
A troubleshooting switch: launches the GPU work of each generation step one kernel at a time instead of replaying a recorded graph. Generation gets slower. Try it when generation crashes or produces garbage while prefill is fine.
Unchecked = don't set the variable.
No effect on Vulkan builds.
Variable: GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1
server-kv-rotation-hint:
Turns off a step (a Hadamard rotation) that keeps a quantized KV cache, such as q8_0 or q4_0, close to f16 quality. Turn it off only to compare quality or speed, or on a backend where it misbehaves; the load logs a warning.
No effect with an f16 or bf16 cache, or a head size that is not a multiple of 64. The DeepSeek-3.2/4, GLM-DSA and dots3note indexers rotate regardless.
Unchecked = rotation on (variable not set).
Variable: LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE=1

instances-failed: The instances could not be read.

instances-not-authorized: The manager refused the web service's request.

field-error-number-min: Enter a whole number of at least {0}.

field-error-gpu-layers: Enter a whole number, auto or all.

api-not-whole-number-in-range: {0} = `{1}` is not a whole number from {2} to {3}

api-instance-bad-label: invalid instance label `{0}`: use 1 to 64 characters with no control character, or leave it empty to remove the label
api-instance-label-taken: the label `{0}` is already used by instance {1}: pick another one
api-load-on-startup-over-max: {0} enabled model profiles would load on startup, but the server loads at most {1} models at once (ModelsMax) and would not start. Turn Load on startup off on another one, or raise ModelsMax
api-load-on-startup-unlimited: {0} enabled model profile(s) would load on startup with ModelsMax = 0, which llama-server rejects at startup (it reads 0 as a limit there, not as unlimited). Set ModelsMax to at least {0}, or turn Load on startup off
api-client-address-in-use: {0} already uses that address and port.
api-client-unresolvable-host: The host name {0} does not resolve to an address.
api-bind-all-with-others: Hostname lists 0.0.0.0 with other addresses; 0.0.0.0 already covers every address, so bind it alone.
api-server-changed-elsewhere: These settings changed elsewhere, or the web service restarted, after you opened them. Reload to see them; your edits here will be lost.
api-model-profile-changed-elsewhere: This model profile changed elsewhere (edited, or switched on or off), or the web service restarted, after you opened it. Reload to see it as it is now; your edits here will be lost.
api-not-json-object: {0} is not a JSON object (a list of "key": value pairs in braces)
api-min-above-max: {0} = {1} is above {2} = {3}: the minimum cannot exceed the maximum
api-server-bad-tags: {0}: the tags {1} are not a list of at most {2} tags, each of {3} to {4} characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, none twice
api-fit-target-format: fit-target `{0}`: {1} as whole numbers, one value or a comma-separated list per device
api-moe-cache-with-tensor-split: moe-cache-mib with split-mode tensor: llama.cpp's MoE cache does not support tensor parallelism and the model would not load. Clear the MoE cache or pick another split mode
api-model-profile-no-model: `{0}` names no model file: every model profile needs a `model` path
api-override-no-pattern: tensor override {0} has an empty pattern
api-override-no-device: tensor override {0} (`{1}`) names no device: a rule is `<pattern>=<device>`, and llama.cpp splits it at the first `=`
api-override-tensor-space: tensor override {0} has a space at the ends of its pattern or its device: llama.cpp keeps it, so the pattern matches no tensor and the device names none. Remove the space
api-override-bad-device: tensor override {0} names `{1}`: a device is a card name of letters, digits and `_` (CPU, ROCm0, CUDA1), and llama.cpp spells the CPU device CPU
api-invalid-model-profile-id: invalid model profile id `{0}`: use letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'
api-model-profile-name-taken: a model profile named `{0}` already exists
api-model-profile-over-memory: `{0}` does not fit the GPU memory of instance `{1}`: it needs {2} MiB, the node has {3} MiB. To make it fit, lower its Context size, or pick a smaller K-cache type or V-cache type (cards Resource / context and KV cache).
api-model-profile-model-missing: `{0}` names a model file that is not there: `{2}` is missing for instance `{1}`. Put the file at that path on the server machine, or change the Model file in pai-config there.
server-edits-dropped: Your unsaved changes were dropped: you signed in with a different account. The form shows the saved settings.
run-ended-failed: llama-server is in the Failed state. Its log on the server says why.
run-timeout: llama-server did not reach the expected state within a minute. The state above keeps updating.
run-timeout-stop: llama-server did not reach the expected state within six minutes. The state above keeps updating.
request-failed: The request did not go through. Try again.
session-ended-retry: Your session has ended. Sign in again, then retry.
api-client-service-failed: The service manager reported an error. The instance's log on the server says why.
boot-toggle: start llama-server when the system starts
boot-hint: Starts llama-server when the system starts, before anyone logs in: the instance's service is enabled (Linux: systemctl enable llama.cpp@default; Windows: its start type is Automatic).
boot-on: llama-server will start when the system starts.
boot-off: llama-server will no longer start when the system starts.
boot-load-failed: Whether llama-server starts at boot could not be read.
model-profiles-intro: Each model profile is one model with its settings. Every instance of the profile's engine can serve it.
model-profiles-load-failed: The model profiles could not be read.
model-profiles-off-note: A model profile switched off is kept, but its engine does not serve it and OpenCode does not offer it.
model-profiles-filter-hint: Matches part of the model profile name or of its model file path. Case does not matter.
model-profiles-no-match: No model profiles match the filter.
model-profiles-switched-on-restart: Switched {0} on: restart the running instances of {1} to apply.
model-profiles-switched-off-restart: Switched {0} off: restart the running instances of {1} to apply.
api-no-model-profile-named: There is no model profile named {0} any more: it was renamed or deleted elsewhere. Open the list of all model profiles again to see them as they are.
model-profile-load-failed: The model profile could not be read.
model-profile-not-found: There is no model profile named {0}.
model-profile-delete-needs-off: To delete this model profile, switch it off first in the list of model profiles.
model-profile-delete-question: Delete the model profile {0}? Its settings are removed, with any unsaved changes on this page. The model file is not deleted. This cannot be undone.
api-model-profile-enabled: {0} is switched on, so it cannot be deleted. Switch it off in the list of model profiles first.
api-model-profile-assigned: {0} is given to the instances {1}, so it cannot be deleted. Remove it from each of them first, on the instance's page; a row set to Off counts too.
delete-unknown: Not confirmed: the manager did not answer in time, so it may or may not have been removed. The list shows it if it is still there.
write-timeout: Not confirmed: the manager did not answer in time, so this may or may not have been done. The page shows what the manager holds once it answers.
model-profile-off: This model profile is switched off: it is kept, but its engine does not serve it. To serve it, switch it on in the list of all model profiles.
model-profile-engine-unavailable: {0} is not available on the server, so no instance can serve this model profile until it is installed again.
model-profile-assets-read-only: The files, Project URL and drafters of a model profile cannot be changed here yet. Change them in pai-config on the server machine.
model-profile-context-size-hint:
How many tokens of conversation the model can hold. Bigger = longer history, more VRAM for the KV cache. It can be divided among requests: see Parallel slots.
Default: 0 (llama.cpp's own), meaning the context the model was trained with.
Flag: --ctx-size
model-profile-parallel-slots-hint:
How many requests can run at once. A number you set DIVIDES the context among them: 2 leaves each request half of Context size.
Default: auto (llama-server's own), 4 slots sharing one KV cache, so one request can use the WHOLE context. Leave it at default to give one request the model's full context.
Flag: --parallel
model-profile-unified-kv-hint:
One KV cache shared by all parallel slots, so any request can grow into the WHOLE context instead of its own share.
On pays off when requests are uneven (one long, others short). Off gives each slot a fixed share, so one long request cannot starve the others.
Default: off with Parallel slots set. With Parallel slots at default, llama-server turns it on anyway, so this is disabled.
Flags: --kv-unified, --no-kv-unified
model-profile-per-slot-context-hint:
Limits every slot to this many tokens. Works with Unified KV on or off.
With Context size at default it also sizes the KV cache as Parallel slots × this value, instead of the model's trained context: 4 slots at 32768 allocate 128k tokens.
Default: no limit.
Flag: --kv-unified-per-slot
model-profile-batch-size-hint:
How many tokens of a prompt are handled per step. Higher speeds up prefill (reading the prompt) and uses more VRAM.
Default: 2048 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --batch-size
model-profile-u-batch-size-hint:
How many tokens are actually computed at once. Must not exceed Batch size.
Default: 512 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --ubatch-size
model-profile-embedding-mode-hint:
Serves this model as an embedding model, turning on /v1/embeddings (without it, llama-server answers 501 "This server does not support embeddings"). Only for dedicated embedding models.
Every input must fit in one batch: set Batch size and U-Batch size above to at least your longest text, or the request fails with "input is too large" (U-Batch size defaults to 512 tokens).
Default: off.
Flag: --embeddings
model-profile-pooling-hint:
How a text's token vectors become ONE embedding. Only used in embedding mode.
Default: the model's own, read from its GGUF.
none = one vector per token; mean = their average; cls = the first token's; last = the last token's (Qwen3-Embedding); rank = the reranker head.
A wrong choice gives no error, only vectors of the right size that search worse.
Flag: --pooling
model-profile-k-cache-type-hint:
Compresses the K half of the KV cache. Lower types use less VRAM but reduce quality.
Default: f16 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --cache-type-k
model-profile-v-cache-type-hint:
Compresses the V half of the KV cache. Lower types use less VRAM but reduce quality; usually set to match K.
A quantized V needs flash attention: with Flash attention off, the model does not load.
Default: f16 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --cache-type-v
model-profile-flash-attention-hint:
A faster attention method: faster prefill and less KV memory.
Default: auto (llama.cpp's own): on wherever the backend supports it.
on forces it. off disables it, which loses most of the gain of a quantized K cache and stops a quantized V cache from loading.
Flag: --flash-attn
model-profile-cache-ram-hint:
How much RAM may hold past prompts for reuse, in MiB, so they need not be read again. Context checkpoints count against it: on a large hybrid model with long prompts and several slots, old prompts are dropped sooner than their KV size suggests.
Default: 8192 MiB (llama.cpp's own). 0 = off, -1 = no limit.
Flag: --cache-ram
model-profile-cache-reuse-hint:
Lets a new prompt reuse matching pieces of the cached one by shifting the KV cache, instead of reading them again. The value is the smallest piece worth reusing, in tokens.
Default: 0, off (llama.cpp's own). llama.cpp also turns it off, with a warning in the log, on a model with an mmproj and on one whose cache cannot shift.
Flag: --cache-reuse
model-profile-context-checkpoints-hint:
How many saved states (checkpoints) each slot keeps, so a prompt that changes partway need not be read again from the start. Matters on recurrent, hybrid and SWA models (Qwen3.5/3.8, qwen4exp, Mamba, Jamba...), which cannot rewind: without checkpoints they read the whole prompt again. No effect on a pure-attention model.
Each checkpoint is a copy of that state in RAM; the oldest is dropped once the slot holds this many.
Default: 32 (llama.cpp's own). 0 = off.
Flag: --ctx-checkpoints
model-profile-checkpoint-step-hint:
The minimum distance between two checkpoints, in tokens. Smaller = a changed prompt resumes closer to the change, but more checkpoints use more RAM (those of a cached prompt also count against Cache RAM).
Default: 8192 (llama.cpp's own). 0 = no minimum.
Flag: --checkpoint-min-step
model-profile-temperature-hint:
How adventurous the output is. Lower = more predictable, higher = more creative.
Default: 0.80 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --temp
model-profile-top-k-hint:
Considers only the K likeliest next tokens. 0 = off.
Default: 40 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --top-k
model-profile-top-p-hint:
Considers only the smallest set of likely tokens whose probabilities add up to P (such as 0.95).
Default: 0.95 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --top-p
model-profile-min-p-hint:
Drops tokens less likely than this fraction of the likeliest one.
Default: 0.05 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --min-p
model-profile-repeat-penalty-hint:
Above 1 discourages repeating recent tokens (such as 1.1).
Default: 1.0, off (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --repeat-penalty
model-profile-presence-penalty-hint:
Positive values discourage any token already seen, pushing toward new topics.
Default: 0.0, off (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --presence-penalty
model-profile-backend-sampling-hint:
Experimental: picks the next token on the GPU that holds the model's output, instead of copying that output to the CPU first.
Only some samplers can run there (greedy, dist, top-k, top-p, min-p, temp, penalties, logit-bias). Any other in the chain (typical, xtc, mirostat, top-n-sigma, dry, adaptive-p) silently sends the WHOLE chain back to the CPU.
Turned off by a grammar or JSON schema, by a Thinking budget, and by split mode tensor. A request asking for pre-sampling probabilities uses the CPU for that request.
Default: off (llama.cpp's own); on is the one value that changes anything. An MTP or DFlash drafter already samples on the GPU, whatever this says.
Flag: --backend-sampling
model-profile-load-on-startup-hint:
Loads this model as soon as the server starts, instead of on its first request. Read only at startup: a model profile added while the server runs is loaded on demand.
The server refuses to start when more model profiles load on startup than ModelsMax allows, and with ModelsMax = 0 whenever any does, so Save refuses that too.
Key: load-on-startup (model profile only, no command-line flag)
model-profile-chat-kwargs-hint:
Extra values passed to the chat template, as JSON, such as {"enable_thinking":true}.
Advanced: leave blank unless the model's documentation lists them.
Flag: --chat-template-kwargs
model-profile-chat-template-hint:
Uses the chat template embedded in the model to format conversations, instead of built-in guesses. Recommended on, for correct tool calls and roles.
Flag: --jinja
model-profile-prefill-assistant-hint:
What to do when a request ends with an assistant message.
On (default, llama.cpp's own): treat it as the start of the reply and continue it, so a client can seed the answer's opening.
Off: treat it as a finished turn and answer it. Turn it off if a client ends on an assistant turn and the model resumes mid-sentence instead of replying.
Flags: --prefill-assistant, --no-prefill-assistant
model-profile-reasoning-hint:
Whether the model thinks before answering.
auto (recommended): follows the model's template.
on: force thinking.
off: disable it.
Flag: --reasoning
model-profile-reasoning-format-hint:
How thinking is delivered to the client.
auto = let the template decide.
deepseek = thinking goes in a separate channel, apart from the answer.
none = left inline in the answer.
Flag: --reasoning-format
model-profile-reasoning-effort-hint:
How hard the template asks the model to think: a level handed to the chat template, neither an on/off switch nor a token limit.
Default: whatever the template does on its own.
Only some templates read it (gpt-oss and harmony do, most do not); the others ignore it silently, and llama-server's log does not say. The Thinking row in Model info is the place that tells you.
Set it here, not in Chat kwargs below: this one setting binds both names templates use (reasoning_effort, reasoning_strength), and a hand-written one sets only one of them.
Flag: --reasoning-effort
model-profile-keep-past-thinking-hint:
Sends the thinking of EVERY past assistant turn back to the model, not just the last one. It costs prompt tokens: the thinking is re-sent every turn.
Default: on (llama.cpp's own). on pins it; off drops it, the one value that changes anything.
Only works where the template supports it: llama-server says so in its log at startup.
Use this, not preserve_thinking or preserve_reasoning in Chat kwargs below: templates read different names, so a hand-written one usually does nothing.
Flags: --reasoning-preserve, --no-reasoning-preserve
model-profile-thinking-budget-hint:
The most tokens the model may spend thinking. Pick it by how long you are willing to wait.
-1 = no limit, 0 = end thinking immediately, N > 0 = that many tokens.
Default: -1 (llama.cpp's own).
At the limit llama.cpp closes the thinking block for the model, which still writes a normal answer. Only works where the template declares thinking tags.
Flag: --reasoning-budget
model-profile-budget-message-hint:
Text added just before thinking is closed at the budget, to steer the model into wrapping up instead of stopping mid-thought. Write it in the language the model answers in: another language invites mixed replies.
Blank = no message (llama.cpp's own default).
No ';' or '#': the INI format cannot escape them, and the value would reload truncated.
Flag: --reasoning-budget-message
model-profile-max-output-hint:
The most tokens one request may generate, thinking and answer together, for clients that do not set their own limit.
-1 = keep going until the context is full.
Default: -1 (llama.cpp's own).
Not a hard limit: a client's own max_tokens always wins, higher or lower.
Flag: --n-predict
model-profile-output-budget-note: The next three split one output budget in two. Thinking budget limits the thinking alone; Max output limits thinking and answer together, so the answer gets what the thinking leaves. Do not copy a model card's numbers as they are: they assume a certain context, and a budget larger than your context never takes effect.
model-profile-vision-on-gpu-hint:
Runs the image encoder (mmproj) on the GPU. On (default, llama.cpp's own), it holds VRAM as long as the model is loaded but only works on image requests. Off: slower image encoding, no VRAM.
Which GPU: see 'Vision GPU' below.
Flags: --mmproj-offload, --no-mmproj-offload
model-profile-vision-offload-toggle: offload the image encoder to GPU
model-profile-vision-gpu-hint:
The GPU the image encoder runs on.
Default: the first GPU in this model profile's device list; with no device checked, the first GPU llama.cpp finds, which on a mixed machine is often not the one running the model. It holds VRAM there and stays idle until an image arrives.
Name a device to override both.
Flag: --mmproj-device
model-profile-vision-off: Used only with an MMProj file, and this model profile has none (Assets).
model-profile-image-tokens-note: The two limits below set how many tokens ONE image takes on dynamic-resolution vision models. They apply only with an MMProj picked above. Leave them at default to read the limit from the model.
model-profile-min-image-tokens-hint:
The fewest tokens each image is encoded to, on vision models with dynamic resolution.
Default: read from the model.
Flag: --image-min-tokens
model-profile-max-image-tokens-hint:
The most tokens each image is encoded to, on vision models with dynamic resolution. Lower it to limit the prefill cost and VRAM of large images.
Default: read from the model.
Flag: --image-max-tokens
model-profile-draft-file-off: Draft device and Draft GPU layers apply only to a Draft model file, and this model profile has none (Assets).
model-profile-moe-later: MoE cache stays as the file has it: its floor needs the model's tensors, which this page does not read yet. Change it in pai-config on the server machine.
model-profile-tensor-placement-intro:
Exceptions to the GPU distribution above: tensors that go on a device of their own, whatever their layer does. On a MoE model, sending the experts of some layers to the CPU frees the most VRAM, as MoE CPU layers does for the first ones. llama.cpp also keeps the embedding table in RAM even when it reports every layer on the GPU: put it on a GPU to reclaim that memory, if the card has room. The first rule that matches a tensor wins.
Key: override-tensor.
model-profile-ot-none: No rules: every tensor goes where its layer goes.
model-profile-ot-format: Layers: empty for every layer, or numbers and ranges such as 10-12, 15. Pattern: a regular expression searched in each tensor's name, such as blk\.1[0-9]\..*_exps.
model-profile-ot-text-hint:
The whole value as llama.cpp reads it: rules <pattern>=<device> joined by commas, the first match winning. Paste a value from a guide here, or change the order of the rules. Applied when you press Enter or leave the field.
Flag: --override-tensor
model-profile-ot-layers-bad: Layers {0} is not a list of layers. Write numbers from 0 to 999 and ranges such as 10-12, 15, at most 256 layers, or leave it empty for every layer.
model-profile-ot-pattern-empty: Write a pattern, or pick a tensor kind.
model-profile-ot-pattern-separator: A pattern cannot hold , or =: llama.cpp splits the rules on them, and neither can be escaped. Write the pattern without them (a range such as {1,2} as a class or an alternative).
model-profile-ot-device-missing: Pick where this rule's tensors go.
model-profile-gpu-layers-hint:
How many of the model's layers run on the GPU. The rest stay on the CPU: less VRAM, slower.
Slider maximum = all layers, once the model file is read.
Default: all layers on the GPU. A model too big for it fails to load, unless Fit to VRAM is on.
Flag: --n-gpu-layers
model-profile-moe-cpu-layers-hint:
Frees VRAM by keeping the experts of this many layers on the CPU; generation gets slower. Only for MoE models: on a dense model use 'Dense FFN CPU layers' below.
Slider maximum = the model's layer count, once the model file is read.
Default: 0, every expert stays on the GPU with its layer.
Flag: --n-cpu-moe
model-profile-moe-cache-hint:
VRAM set aside for recently used experts kept in RAM, so a token that needs them reads them from the card instead of over PCIe. Experimental.
It only acts on layers whose experts are ALL in RAM (MoE CPU layers above, or an exps=CPU Tensor placement rule); with none, llama.cpp runs without a cache.
With several GPUs the budget is split like the layers: by Tensor split, or by free VRAM when that is blank.
The model FAILS TO LOAD under Split mode tensor, and below the experts of one token.
The draft model never uses it, and the synthetic benchmark cannot measure it.
Default: 0, no cache (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --moe-cache-mib
model-profile-dense-ffn-cpu-layers-hint:
Frees VRAM by keeping the feed-forward weights (most of a layer's size) of the first N layers on the CPU; attention stays on the GPU. For dense models: on a MoE model it reaches only the dense layers such a model may have, never the experts.
Default: every feed-forward weight stays on the GPU with its layer.
Flag: --n-cpu-ffn
model-profile-op-offload-hint:
Whether work on weights kept in RAM is still sent to the GPU. Worth trying when experts or other tensors are in RAM and the card sits on a narrow PCIe link: off then prefills faster, because those weights are no longer copied to the card on every prefill batch (the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next guide has the figures). Decode does not change.
Default: on (llama.cpp's own); off is the one value that changes anything. No effect when every weight is in VRAM.
Flags: --op-offload, --no-op-offload
model-profile-repack-hint:
When loading, rearranges weights kept in RAM into the layout the CPU's fast kernels use, for the types it has them for (x86 AVX2: Q4_0, Q4_K, IQ4_NL, MXFP4; Q2_K with AVX-512).
Only matters without a GPU, or with No host buffer on: with a GPU, weights in RAM go to its host buffer and this does nothing.
Default: on (llama.cpp's own); off is the one value that changes anything. No effect when no weight is in RAM.
Flags: --repack, --no-repack
model-profile-no-host-buffer-hint:
Keeps weights left in RAM in ordinary memory instead of the GPU's pinned host buffer (RAM locked in place, which the GPU reads directly).
Off (default, llama.cpp's own): pinned.
On: ordinary, pageable RAM, and the CPU repacks the types it can (see Repack). The copies Op offload makes then come from pageable memory, and repacked experts leave the MoE cache.
No effect when no weight is in RAM.
Flag: --no-host
model-profile-lazy-tensors-hint:
Saves RAM on models with very large tables: reads them from disk as needed, a row per token, instead of keeping them in memory. Only a few architectures have such tables (such as gemma4 and qwen4exp); no effect on others. Keep the GGUF on an SSD.
Default: auto (llama.cpp's own): lazy only for a table over 4 GiB, and off if one of the model's devices cannot memory-map (an integrated GPU).
on = lazy whatever the size and the devices; off = always in RAM (no disk reads, but all of the RAM).
Works whatever Load mode says.
Flag: --lazy-mode
model-profile-load-mode-hint:
How this model's weights get into memory. Pick one: the modes do not combine.
Default: auto (llama.cpp's own).
auto: memory-maps the file (reads it on demand) unless a device can't; fastest to load.
none: reads the weights into RAM up front: slower, uses the model's size in RAM, but nothing can be dropped back to the file.
mmap: always memory-maps.
mlock: locks the weights in physical RAM WITHOUT memory-mapping: steady latency, needs room for the whole model.
mmap+mlock: memory-maps and locks what it maps.
dio: Direct I/O where the platform offers it.
Lazy tensors stay mapped whatever this says.
Flag: --load-mode
model-profile-fit-to-vram-hint:
Lets llama.cpp pick the context size and GPU layers that fit your GPU memory, leaving about 1 GiB free on each GPU.
On by default, as in llama.cpp. For a full fit, leave Context size and GPU layers at default.
When on, also leave tensor-split, Tensor placement, MoE CPU layers and Dense FFN CPU layers empty: with any of them llama.cpp fits only the context (the log warns), which can over-fill one card.
Flag: -fit
model-profile-fit-allowed: auto-fit context and layers to device memory (-fit on)
model-profile-fit-not-allowed: needs Context size and GPU layers at default
model-profile-fit-invalid: llama-server refuses this value, so it cannot run this model profile. Use on or off.
model-profile-fit-layers-only: auto-fit the GPU layers only: Context size is set (-fit on)
model-profile-fit-context-only: auto-fit the context only: GPU layers is set, so llama.cpp keeps your layers (-fit on)
model-profile-fit-nothing: nothing to fit: Context size and GPU layers are both set (-fit on)
model-profile-fit-min-context-hint:
The smallest context Fit to VRAM may cut down to. Only used with Fit to VRAM on.
Default: 4096 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --fit-ctx
model-profile-fit-free-vram-hint:
How much VRAM Fit to VRAM leaves free, in MiB: one number for every device, or a comma-separated list in device order (such as 2048,1024). Only used with Fit to VRAM on.
Blank = 1024 per device (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --fit-target
model-profile-draft-device-hint:
The GPU for a separate draft model file. Pin it to ONE device: MTP heads crash on an automatic multi-GPU split.
A full-vocabulary DFlash or DSpark drafter under a layer split must sit on the GPU with the last layers, or it aborts at load; picking the file pins it there for you.
Disabled with built-in MTP heads, which share the main model's GPU.
Blank = automatic, same as the model.
Flag: --device-draft
model-profile-draft-gpu-layers-hint:
How many layers of a separate draft model file run on the GPU.
For an MTP head file, which has no layers, 99 puts the draft on the GPU and 0 on the CPU.
Pin a device above: MTP heads crash on an automatic multi-GPU split.
Disabled with built-in MTP heads.
Default: all draft layers on the GPU.
Flag: --n-gpu-layers-draft
model-profile-draft-n-max-hint:
The most tokens a draft proposes per step. DFlash limits this to the size it was trained for, minus one (the Draft file row shows it).
Default: 3 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-draft-n-max
model-profile-draft-p-min-hint:
How sure the drafter must be, 0 to 1. Drafting stops at the first token below this, so the model checks a shorter batch instead of tokens it would reject.
Default: 0, never stops early (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-draft-p-min
model-profile-draft-n-min-hint:
The shortest draft worth checking. A shorter one, usually cut by Draft p-min, is thrown away, and that step generates one token normally. Raise it when short drafts cost more to check than they save.
Default: 0, keeps any length (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-draft-n-min
model-profile-draft-n-ubatch-hint:
How many tokens the draft computes at once. Smaller spares VRAM, at the cost of more passes when the drafter catches up on a long prompt. Applies to built-in MTP heads too.
Default: 0, the model's U-Batch size (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-draft-n-ubatch
model-profile-draft-cache-note: The draft keeps its OWN KV cache, which does not follow the model's: it stays at f16 unless you set it here. Quantize it to reclaim VRAM. Unlike the placement settings above, these two also apply to MTP heads built into the main model.
model-profile-draft-k-cache-type-hint:
Compresses the K half of the draft's KV cache. A draft context is small, so this matters most with a separate draft model and a large context.
Default: f16, NOT the model's K-cache type.
Flag: --spec-draft-type-k
model-profile-draft-v-cache-type-hint:
Compresses the V half of the draft's KV cache. Usually matched to Draft K-cache type. A quantized V needs flash attention.
Default: f16, NOT the model's V-cache type.
Flag: --spec-draft-type-v
model-profile-match-length-hint:
How many recent tokens must match before a draft is proposed. Below 16, llama.cpp warns that drafts may be poor.
Default: 24 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-mod-n-match
model-profile-min-draft-hint:
The fewest tokens a draft must have to be proposed, 0 to 1024.
Default: 48 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-mod-n-min
model-profile-max-draft-hint:
The most tokens drafted per step, 0 to 1024.
Default: 64 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-mod-n-max
model-profile-ngram-simple-lookup-hint:
How many recent tokens are looked up in the context (the n-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 12 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-simple-size-n
model-profile-ngram-simple-draft-hint:
How many tokens are drafted after a match (the m-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 48 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-simple-size-m
model-profile-ngram-map-lookup-hint:
How many recent tokens are looked up in the context (the n-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 12 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-map-k-size-n
model-profile-ngram-map-draft-hint:
How many tokens are drafted after a match (the m-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 48 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-map-k-size-m
model-profile-ngram-map-values-lookup-hi:
How many recent tokens are looked up in the context (the n-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 12 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-n
model-profile-ngram-map-values-draft-hin:
How many tokens are drafted after a match (the m-gram), 1 to 1024.
Default: 48 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-map-k4v-size-m
model-profile-min-hits-hint:
How many times an n-gram must have been seen before what follows it is proposed. Higher drafts less often but more reliably.
Default: 1 (llama.cpp's own).
Flag: --spec-ngram-map-k4v-min-hits
model-profile-draft-group-off: Used only with a draft: a Draft model or a Drafter, and this model profile has neither (Assets).
model-profile-ngram-off: Used only when N-gram drafters (Assets) includes {0}.
model-profile-gpu-distribution-intro:
Which GPUs run THIS model and how much each holds, saved to models.ini. Check nothing to let llama.cpp choose. With two GPUs of different sizes, check both and give the bigger one more; left on Auto, the split follows free VRAM at load, not an even cut. Under split mode layer, once the model file is read, each GPU takes a number of blocks: the model's blocks and its output layer, shared out top to bottom. Otherwise the weights are ratios: 3 and 1 give 75% and 25%. The checked GPUs, top to bottom, are the split order: Move up and Move down change it; the first one is llama.cpp's main GPU.
Keys: split-mode, device, tensor-split.
model-profile-model-facts-moe: Model file: {0} blocks, with experts: {1} per layer, {2} used per token.
model-profile-model-facts-none: No layer counts: {0}. The GPU weights stay ratios, and the layer fields have no slider.
model-profile-model-facts-failed: The model file's layer counts could not be read. The GPU weights stay ratios, and the layer fields have no slider; open the page again to retry.
api-model-info-fetched: its model is fetched at startup (`{0}`), so its layer facts are unknown until it is downloaded
api-model-info-missing: the model file `{0}` is not there
api-model-info-unreadable: `{0}` is not a readable model file
model-profile-gpu-blocks-budget: The checked GPUs share {0} places: {1} blocks and the output layer.
model-profile-gpu-blocks-auto: Auto: llama.cpp shares the {0} places by free memory at load. Choose Even to set the blocks yourself.
model-profile-gpu-blocks-malformed: tensor-split {0} is not a list of numbers of 0 or more. Choose Even to set the blocks yourself, or Auto.
model-profile-moe-reading: Reading the model file to see whether it has experts…
model-profile-moe-dense: This model has no experts (a dense model), so MoE CPU layers does nothing for it. Use Dense FFN CPU layers below.
model-profile-split-mode-hint:
How THIS model is divided between GPUs. Does nothing with one GPU checked. Same on CUDA and ROCm.
layer (default): each GPU takes a consecutive run of blocks, in the proportion of its weight. Fastest prefill; copes with a slow link between GPUs.
none: one GPU, the first checked row; other checked rows go unused.
tensor (experimental): the GPUs act as one device, and all weights and the KV cache are divided by the ratio (blank = even). Fastest decode, needs a fast link. Flash attention must not be off, Fit to VRAM is skipped (set Context size yourself), some architectures refuse to load, and llama.cpp tunes it for CUDA with no guarantees on other backends.
row (deprecated, use tensor): weights are split by rows by the ratio (CUDA/ROCm; Vulkan falls back to layer). The KV cache follows the layer cut.
Flag: --split-mode
model-profile-gpu-failed: The host's GPU list could not be read. The GPUs this profile names are shown; to add another, open the page again.
model-profile-gpu-no-probe: No GPU list: the engine's device probe gave no answer on this host.
model-profile-gpu-none-found: No GPU found on this host.
api-device-bad-name: {0}: `{1}` is not a device llama.cpp accepts: no spaces, none of ; # =, not CPU, and none only alone
api-model-profile-device-outside: {2} = {3} names a GPU outside the Devices of instance {1}'s server profile, so model profile {0} may not use it. Pick a GPU of those Devices, or widen the server profile's Devices first
model-profile-gpu-weights-incomplete: Give every checked GPU a weight of 0 or more, or clear them all for Auto.
model-profile-gpu-split-without-device: This profile's tensor-split {0} applies to every GPU llama.cpp finds, in its order. Checking GPUs here replaces it.
api-tensor-split-format: tensor-split = `{0}` is not a list of up to 15 numbers of 0 or more, separated by , or /
about-failed: The versions could not be read.
about-no-engine: No installed engine was found on this host. An engine package from before this version lists none until it is installed again.
node-failed: The node's information could not be read.
node-gpus-none: No GPU was found on this node.
node-info-unavailable: The manager did not answer, so the operating system, the kernel and the GPUs are not shown. Reload the page to try again.
node-info-failed: The manager could not read the operating system, the kernel and the GPUs.
node-driver-in-kernel: (part of the kernel, so its version is the kernel's)
